is an expreess line of Peckern Transit in Los Sengas. This line currently has 5 stations, and runs between and .

Description

is an east-west oriented express line of Peckern Transit in Los Sengas, and runs between Festival and Flask. Subsequent development will see this line providing direct services with .

This line is represented by light blue on the Route Map, and is Line Number 4.

History

Kasukano Train Railway Era (New Peckern Express)

  • January 22 2017: Plans for this line surfaced.
  • April 8 2017: The section between New Phantasm and began services.
  • April 11 2017: The section between and began services.

Peckern Transit Era (New Peckern Express)

  • May 1 2017: Kasukano Train Railway shuts down, and this line is taken over by Los Sengas Government.
  • May 6 2017: Peckern Transit is established and takes over this line.
  • June 4 2018: This line became a part of the Co-Op Railway.
  • December 21 2018: A player connected tracks between Metropolis and Cyanland without the operator's permission. However, the tracks have since been demolished by the administrator.

'''Pelos Metrolink''' Era

  • August 2 2020: After 3 years, this line is officially renamed '''Pelos Metrolink'''.
  • August 2020: New Phantasm Station has been renamed Cylupus Valley Station and was rebuilt. As a result, the destination of has been changed to Kanjono de Maho Station (Subsequently Renamed Woyi Gap Station).

Era

  • September 21 2023: After '''Peckern Metro''' is renamed Peckern Transit, this line is renamed '''Metro Line''' to allude to the theme of "Bustling City", as well as the name of with which it provides Through Service.

Districts Served

  • Festival
  • Peckern
  • West Metropolis Archipelago (Passes Through)
  • Downtown
  • Katadelphia
  • Flask

Line Characteristics

  • This line is one of the two lines that passes through West Metropolis Archipelago without any stations in the area (The other line being ), and is also the only line that provides direct access between Peckern and Downtown.
  • The Grand Squirrel-Metropolis CHT between and is currently the longest underwater tunnel in Los Sengas.

Fun Facts

  • The eastbound Platform 1 and westbound Platform 2 of Metropolis Terminal, which are used by this line, are managed by Nazca Railway and constructed by Nazca Railway alongside platforms 33-40 of Metropolis Terminal in the Phase IV expansion while featuring in-fare zone interchange. At the time of construction, this set of platforms were numbered 41 (Eastbound) and 42 (Westbound), but due to the construction of Phase V and platforms 41-48, the platforms are re-numbered.
  • Among all the lines that serve Metropolis Terminal, this line is the only line which is not operated by Nazca Railway. However, the platforms that serve this line have been in use since the Kasukano Train Railway-era when this line was named '''New Peckern Express'''.

title: Metropolis Forest Park
safeHtml:
'''Metropolis Forest Park''' is a forest park constructed by Deepond Industry, which is located at No. 15 Temple Street.

History

  • July 22 2016: The land at No. 15 Temple Street started bidding.
  • August 1 2016: The land at No. 15 Temple Street was won by Yangdazhi0903, William_SkyWalk, and Chardylee2004.
  • August 5 2016: The commencement of the Metropolis Forest Park was delayed.
  • August 19 2016: The general design plan was released, and the Metropolis Forest Park construction began.
  • September 12 2016: The Los Sengas Government agreed to recruit assistants.
  • September 23 2016: The Metropolis Forest Park recruited staff, and CoreIsHeart, Reaganc86, and TR6156justin were awarded development assistance rights.
  • October 29 2016: The Metropolis Forest Park was completed.

  • This station is the first station in Los Sengas Division, as well as the first Terminal-class station.
  • This station has the most exits of any NR Station.
  • This station features the most lines of any NR Station.
  • This station is the first station to be built in 2015, as well as the first to expand in 2016, 2017 and 2022.
  • Platforms 49 and 50 of this station were originally numbered Platforms 41 and 42. However, following the dissolution of Kasukano Train Railway (Los Sengas) and the construction of Phase V, there are renumbered Platforms 1, 2 of Peckern Transit to avoid confusion. Then, after the takeover of Peckern Metro by Nazca Railway (Which is subsequently renamed Peckern Transit by NR) and the construction of Phase VII, the platforms are once again renumbered to their current platform numbers.
  • Prior to the Phase VII Expansion, Platforms 49 and 50 (Then Platforms 1 and 2 of Peckern Metro) were only connected to the Phase IV Concourse by a makeshift passageway.
  • After the completion of Phase VI, the platform number of this station has reached 58, but Platforms 49 and 50 remained unused until the numbers were used by Peckern Transit .
  • While Platforms 39 and 40 are built as a part of Phase IV and was originally reserved for use, it was ultimately used by and became a part of Phase VII.

  • The Colors of the Zones in this Underground Walkway pay tribute to the Underground Walkway System in East Tsim Sha Tsui Station of the Mass Transit Railway System in Hong Kong with regards that both Underground Walkway Zones have Red, Yellow and Green Zones. However, due to the number of exits in this Underground Walkway System, the Blue Zone is added in addition to the three colors. title: Miner Bay Depot
safeHtml:
'''Miner Bay Depot''' is one of the depots of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division. It is located at Miner Bay of Tripaw Peninsula. This Depot provides services for , , , , , , , , , , , , and . This depot was formerly the largest depot in Nazca Railway, but was later taken over by the Vector Bay Depot of the . This depot can store up to 60 trains, featuring 30 sidings, ten 204 m long, ten 408 m long and ten 612 m long.

Description

Miner Bay Depot is located to the south of Miner North Station and the north of Tai Wan Peninsula Station.

Depot Structure

Stabling Sidings

  • Two Sets of Outer Sidings
  • Each outer siding has ten siding tracks.
  • One set of Central Sidings that has ten siding tracks.
  • Two Sets of Inner Sidings
  • Each inner siding has ten siding tracks.
  • Depot Platforms and Maintenance Pits.
  • The Following Sidings are not connected to the southward tracks:
  • Coast Sidings: Features a total of ten sidings.
  • Bay Sidings
  • Loading Sidings

Depot Platforms

  • A pair of Standard Length (204 m) Island Platforms.
  • Does not feature Platform Screen Doors.

Maintenance Pit

Loading Sidings

  • This is where new trains in Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division are loaded. Operates in a similar fashion to Metro-Vector-Paw Container Terminals.

Connecting Tracks

The Depot has two sets of tracks connecting to the railway network, one to the north and one to the south:

  • North Entrance: Directly connected to Miner North Station Platforms 2, 3 for convenience of train services.
  • South Entrance: Feature Sidings connected to tracks. In turn, the main tracks are connected to the shared , tracks.

Fun Facts

  • This depot is currently the third largest depot in Nazca Railway, and is currently the main operations center in Los Sengas Division.
  • This depot expanded after the completion of , Tai Wan Peninsula Station.
